overview: Preparation for the digital SAT Math section, run as a test-review-retest loop: a full adaptive practice SAT sets your baseline, your tutor walks you through every question you missed and gives you fresh practice on each weak skill, then you retest with all-new questions and watch your score move.
naturalProgression: Lock in linear equations, functions, systems and inequalities (Algebra)
Master equivalent expressions, quadratics, exponentials and nonlinear equations (Advanced Math)
Read data with confidence: rates, percentages, scatterplots, probability and inference (Problem-Solving & Data Analysis)
Cover area, volume, triangles, trigonometry and circles (Geometry & Trigonometry)
Use Desmos, grid-in rules and two-module pacing the way top scorers do

examAlignment.format: Two adaptive 22-question modules; multiple choice (4 options) and student-produced response
examAlignment.calculator: Desmos graphing calculator permitted for the entire section

aiInstructionModel.approach: Test, review every miss with the tutor, transfer practice, retest
aiInstructionModel.description: The student's own misses are the curriculum. The tutor reviews one missed question at a time — diagnose the error, reteach only what is missing, show the fastest SAT method (including when to graph it in Desmos) — then gives fresh practice on the same skill before moving on. When the review is done, the student retests with all-new questions.

aiGuidanceNotes: For SAT prep, every review ends in the fastest reliable method a student can use under time. Teach Desmos as a first-class tool — graph to solve systems, find intersections, zeros and vertices, and run regressions — but make sure the student can also do it by hand when graphing is slower. Grid-in answers must follow the entry rules (5 characters, 6 with a minus sign; fractions or decimals; no mixed numbers). Module 1 decides whether Module 2 is the harder version, so careful work early is worth more than speed. Never reveal an answer before the student has tried the question.
